about.title: La Habra Heights Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: La Habra Heights is a quiet, hillside community, but its winding roads still see collisions worth taking seriously. Public records show 12 injury collisions and 14 injured people in the most recent year, with reported crashes clustering on Tuesday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. — often along Harbor Boulevard, Hacienda Road, East Road, and Harbor Road. Whether you were driving, a passenger, or on a bike near one of these corridors, the aftermath can bring medical bills, missed work, and insurance calls you didn't ask for. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent personal injury attorney in the network who can review what happened and explain your options under California law. Acting early matters: evidence like skid marks, dashcam footage, and witness memories fade fast, and insurers often reach out before you've had time to think. Getting guidance early can help protect your position from the start.

whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Before Talking to the Insurer

items.title: The Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the crash date to file a claim, but that window shrinks to as little as six months if a government entity — like a road authority — may be at fault. Waiting too long can cost you the right to recover anything at all.

items.title: Comparative Fault Can Work Against You
items.desc: California uses pure comparative fault, meaning your compensation can be reduced by whatever percentage of blame the insurer assigns to you. An early, careless statement to an adjuster can be used to inflate that percentage.

items.title: No Fee Unless You Recover
items.desc: Attorneys in the network work on contingency, so there's no upfront cost to get answers about your situation. You only pay a fee if there's a recovery, which is why getting a free case review costs you nothing to consider.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers often use those statements to look for phrases that shift blame onto you, which matters under California's comparative fault rules. An independent attorney can advise you on what, if anything, to say.

items.question: Are there specific roads in La Habra Heights where these crashes tend to happen?
items.answer: Public collision records point to Harbor Boulevard, Hacienda Road, East Road, and Harbor Road as higher-volume corridors, with Tuesday evenings between 6 and 8 p.m. showing more reported crashes than other times. This doesn't mean any of these roads are unsafe — it simply reflects where and when collisions have been recorded.

items.question: What if the crash involved a city vehicle or happened on a road maintained by a government agency?
items.answer: Claims against government entities in California often carry a much shorter filing deadline — sometimes as little as six months instead of the usual two years. Because these claims involve extra procedural steps, it's worth getting an attorney's input quickly if you suspect a public agency may be involved.

items.question: Is there really no cost to use LawProactive?
items.answer: Correct — LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent personal injury attorney; we are not a law firm ourselves. Attorneys in the network work on contingency, meaning they only collect a fee if you recover compensation.
